full_judgment: 2. The facts, leading to filing of this Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal, in short, are that, the present respondent No.1 herein as writ petitioner filed Writ Petition No.11692 of 2016 before the High Court Division for declaring the refusal of the registration of the writ petitioner in the Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council and decision for non registering the writ petitioner in the MBBS course in future by the writ respondent Nos.3 and 4 through issuing a letter dated 11.08.2016 to the writ petitioner barring him from any future Medical Education (Annexures-E, E-1 and E-2) which are without lawful authority and are of no legal effect and giving direction upon the writ respondent Nos. 2-4 for issuing registration as an admitted student in the MBBS Course of 2013-2014 Session and giving him per-mission for attending classes of the afore-said course stating inter alia that the writ petitioner, with a brilliant academic career, having secured GPA 5M0 both in his Secondary School Certificate (SSC) and Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations, applied on 04.10.2013 for admission to the MBBS Course in the year 2013-2014 and his roll number was 300829. The writ petitioner sat for the test and the result was published by writ respondent No.2 showing that the writ petitioner had obtained test score of 45.5 merit Score of 145.5 and his position in the merit list was 22250. Subsequently, the writ petitioner appeared for the admission test for the MBBS course at Gonoshasthaya Samaj Vittik Medical College (hereinafter referred to as the College) and his roll number was 306. The said examination was conducted by the writ respondent No.4. On being successful in the admission test, the writ petitioner was admitted in the first year of the MBBS Course in the college. The writ petitioner completed his Course and successfully passed the First Professional Examination (both written and viva). Thereafter, the writ petitioner duly appeared in the second professional examination of the MBBS course, but his result was withheld. Upon making queries, it transpired that the writ respondent No.3 had sent two letters on 11.02.2016 to writ respondent No.4 stating that the information which was sent by the College with regard to the writ petitioner's merit score and merit position was inconsistent with the information sent by the Directorate of Health and accordingly, a clarification was sought from the College in this regard. Subsequently, vide letter dated 13.06.2016 (Annexure E-1) Bangladesh Medical Dental Council (briefly, BMDC) informed the Principal of the College that the writ petitioner had obtained his admission in the MBBS course for 2013-2014 by providing incorrect information and on that ground, the Council had declined to grant registration to the writ petitioner. It was further stated that no registration would be granted to the writ petitioner in future. Subsequently, vide Memo dated 11.08.2016 (Annexure-E-2), the Principal of the College intimated the decision of BMDC to the concerned members of the Faculty in the College. Under the afore-said facts and circumstances, the writ petitioner served a legal notice upon the writ respondents seeking redress but in vain. Hence, the writ petitioner, finding no other alternative efficacious remedy, filed the instant writ petition before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule Nisi.
